utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us whose signature appears here?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Again, my signature appears on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does the date which is recorded herein accurately state the date that you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, the date reflects the date when I signed the document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, subsequent to signing this statement, did you have occasion to review the same in Serbian to check if everything is accurately recorded therein?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to move to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I reviewed the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please move a bit more to the microphone or have the microphone adjusted so that it's closer to your mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to turn to page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would like to look at paragraph number 6 with you, sir. And I would ask you, sir, to please advise the Chamber of the correction that you wish to make to this paragraph of your statement.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Could this be zoomed in a little for my benefit so I can actually see it better?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The part in question should be the fourth line from the bottom in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes. What I would like to correct here is the sentence reading: "They first informed me ..." And then "the police station in Kljuc ..." I would like to change this. The sentence as I would like it to be corrected should read: "These forest workers informed first the police station in Kljuc and then me."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could look at paragraph 7 on the same page in English, and it will be on the next page in the Serbian, I would ask you, sir, to please advise of what correction is necessary in this page -- in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph, in the sentence reading as follows: "Six soldiers were killed and around 30 were wounded." This should read: "Around six soldiers were killed ..." I didn't know the exact number. I just knew that it was a close approximation of the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now paragraph 10, which is on the same page, what correction is necessary that you would like to bring to our attention in relation to this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: In the sentence which reads: "This thwarted all sorts of traffic in that direction." The correction should be made in the following sense: "The traffic in that direction was rendered more difficult by that."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now apart from these corrections that we have gone through in court, do you stand by the rest of your statement as accurately and correctly setting forth your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by everything in this statement. I consider everything to be truthful and credible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I -- I just have a question on this very last paragraph. Sir, does it mean, in fact, that traffic in the opposite direction was safe, it was usable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The traffic did take place but it was much slower in that place because the road had been dug out. Not enough explosive had been placed in that spot, and it was not placed in such a way that a passing car could activate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm interested in is in the opposite direction. Was traffic moving in the opposite direction in any manner disturbed or wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In both directions, traffic was disturbed because all the passing vehicles had to slow down and drive over that spot that had been dug out very slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we then to understand that, in fact, you would like to change the statement to say traffic was disturbed on that road -- on that part of the road, irrespective of direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it was rendered more difficult or disturbed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I were to ask you questions based upon the same topics as contained in your statement today, would your answers to my questions be the same as is recorded in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, my answers would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, given that you've taken a solemn declaration today, would that mean that the answers, including what is recorded in your statement, are truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, my answers are truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would tender this statement has the next public exhibit. There are no associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, before we decide, may I take it that the reference to -- I think it was on paragraph 10 of the 92 ter motion about Sanski Most, et cetera, that that's a mistake rather than the statement being a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would advise to carefully read a motion before it's signed. You didn't sign it, so -- but having clarified this matter, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1617 receives number D867, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have a short summary. Witness Rajko Kalabic was elected during the first multiparty elections in 1990 as a deputy of the chamber of municipalities of the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina from Kljuc municipality. In Kljuc, the SDS received over 50 per cent of the vote and the SDA about 20 per cent of the vote. Despite this, the key posts in the local government were distributed equally among Serb and Muslim personnel. The president of the municipal assembly was a Serb. As early as 1991, the Muslims formed the Donji Kraji Muslim municipality of Kljuc. Although they formed their own municipality, they still went to work in Kljuc and received their salaries. This was the case until 27 May 1992, when Muslims failed to turn up for work. That same day, Deputy Police Commander Stojakovic was ambushed and killed at Krasulje and several police were injured at the hands of the Muslims. That same day the army was also under attack as several buses of unarmed soldiers was attacked by men under the command of Omer Filipovic, a Muslim. The road was also mined between Laniste and Velagici. A Serb driver was hanged and killed by the roadside at Pudin Han. This series of attacks sparked a revolt among the Serb population. After these events, a unit of the VRS under the command of Colonel Galic came from the Kula barracks near Mrkonjic Grad. Weapons were collected in the villages where Omer Filipovic had his paramilitary units. During the fighting between the VRS and Muslim paramilitaries, the civilian Muslim population was invited over the radio to take shelter in the town of Kljuc, and after the end of combat the municipal authorities put them on buses and returned them to their home villages. This completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to turn together to page 2 of your statement and paragraph 1 of the same, which specifies that you were employed as director of forest management at Sip before the war. Could you please tell us what was your professional occupation during the war?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was the manager of the 1st Company within the Sipad-Kljuc enterprise. I was then elected as a deputy in the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As a volunteer. I was not a professional politician, that is. And then during the war, by virtue of my position as a deputy in the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which then became Republika Srpska, I was a member of the Crisis Staff of the municipality, again as a volunteer, not as a professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, the work which you performed within the Crisis Staff of Kljuc, was that a full-time position?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: No. It was a voluntary position. It was a temporary engagement. I had to attend meetings called by the president of the Crisis Staff or the president of the municipality. When such a meeting was called, if I could I would attend such a meeting, and if I am indisposed, then I would say so. I would give the reasons why I couldn't attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to move to page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would like to look at paragraph 5 of your statement. Can you tell us, sir, whose proposal was it to split the executive positions in the local government 50/50 despite the overwhelming SDS victory in the votes?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: The SDS leadership proposed the positions in Kljuc municipality should be distributed proportionally, 50 per cent for the SDS and 50 per cent for the SDA. And that was how things were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the objective behind this proposal?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: The objective of such a proposal was to honour the SDS position on the necessity to have a good co-operation between the parties in power so as to ensure that the life in the municipality continued normally. In other words, every possibility of discrimination was avoided, or rather there was an attempt made to avoid any possible form of discrimination in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to move now to page 4 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would like to focus on paragraph 14 of your statement. Can you please perhaps explain for us what you meant to convey -- what information you meant to convey in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see paragraph 4, please, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 14 it should be, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this paragraph, I wanted to say that what happened on the 27th of May, 1992, was not an accident. Everything had been planned in advance. The SDA leadership knew that a significant number of the Serbian soldiers were outside of Kljuc either in training in Zenica, which is 30 kilometres away from Kljuc, or were reassigned to some other units which were far away from Kljuc. It was a suitable moment because the VRS army was not nearby to do what was done on the 27th of May. On the 27th of May, a police patrol was intercepted and the deputy commander of the police was killed, and a convoy of young recruits was attacked as they were returning from having served in the army and they were on their way back to Serbia, Montenegro, and other parts of the former Yugoslavia. They had served as recruits in the JNA. They had done their service and they were on their way home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to look at page 5 in English and 6 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would like to focus on paragraph 22 of your statement. Here you talk of how all police officers were asked to remain at their jobs despite their ethnicity, but many Muslims were not prepared to preserve the Republika Srpska. Do you recall any examples of non-Serbs that remained in the police in Kljuc municipality?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Amongst the police in the Kljuc municipality, there was a person in uniform, a Croat, who stayed on the force until the end of the war. And after the war, he continued working in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall any other non-Serbs that stayed in important positions and jobs within Kljuc municipality during the war?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, until the end of the war also a Croat stayed on as secretary in SIK Kljuc, which is a prominent position as well, and also a Muslim stayed on -- or, rather, several Muslims stayed on in SIK Kljuc, at the post office, and in some other companies. However, some people stayed until the end of the war, and a number of these people went abroad, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall any non-Serbs in Kljuc municipality who were serving in the VRS in any capacity?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean, there were several Muslims and Croats who served in the army or were, rather, part of the Army of Republika Srpska until the end of the war. Some of them did stay, but a Croat held the most prominent position. He was a captain. He stayed in the Army of Republika Srpska until the end of the war, and after the war he remained in Kljuc and he had this job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could we try to be a bit more concrete. For both categories, that is, those, you said, prominent positions in -- I think you specifically mentioned secretary of SIK, post office, you said: "Some people stayed until the end war, and a number of these people went abroad, Switzerland, Austria, Germany." Now, could you tell us how many stayed until the end of the war? Was it 1, was it 10, was it 50, was it a hundred? How many stayed up until the end of the war of this category?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the end of the war, that is to say until the end of the war, there was this captain in the army, that's to say, he didn't go anywhere --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and the secretary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I split up the two categories. I'm first asking about the first category; that is, the category in which the secretary of the SIK and the post office people were there, how many of those stayed in their prominent positions until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until he retired, the secretary from Sip stayed on. During the war, he managed to have enough years for retirement and then he retired and stayed in Kljuc, and then there were other people who worked throughout the war, kept their jobs. They did not hold prominent positions, but they had certain office jobs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do I then well understand from those holding prominent positions, that one remained but retired during the war and that not any other prominent person remained in that position until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the second category; that is, those serving in the VRS. You told us about a Croatian captain who stayed until the end of the war and then even stayed after the war on the VRS. How many others were staying there in the VRS throughout the war? Non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact number, but a small number were there certainly throughout the war, in the Army of Republika Srpska. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know any other person by name or you say ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot -- I cannot remember any names now because it's really been a very long, long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So concretely we have only one person in a prominent position, secretary of the Sip, who retired during the war, so therefore did not stay until the end of the war in his position, and concretely you can tell us about one Croatian officer of Kljuc that remained in the VRS throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And I said that a policeman also stayed on in the police force until the end of the war and continued to work in the police after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that policeman very well. His last name was Modric. I cannot remember his first name now. Zdeno -- Zdenko, I've just remembered now. Zdenko Modric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to look at paragraph 20 on the same page in English but on the prior page in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I suspect it's the same problem that the back is having with e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: E-court is not functioning at this moment. We are waiting for ITSS to assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's also what my staff told me. Let me see if there is any questions that do not relate to the statement. Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can move to a question that does not need e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise you could perhaps quote from the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, I could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's easy enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 20 of your statement, you talk about attempts that were made to try to prevent incidents of plunder and crime. Could you tell us what specific measures were attempted by the municipal authorities to try to prevent incidents of plunder and crime?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: The municipal authorities asked the police and army to protect buildings, facilities in villages, and also the population in villages where there were no war operations, and that was done in the villages that were on the other side of Kljuc in relation to the villages where there were war operations going on, and these villages are the following: Dubocanin, Velecevo, Zgon, and Mehmedagici. In these villages, both the buildings and the population were protected. At that point in time, the population was still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, if you could help us for these villages that you have identified, what would have been the ethnicity of the inhabitants of those villages?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: In these villages, the population was Muslim only except for Mehmedagici. In Mehmedagici, about 10 per cent of the population was of a different ethnic background; Serb or Croat, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I would like to ask you if you had any -- if you had the occasion to learn at any time of any killings of detained Muslims that occurred 1st June 1992 in relation to the village of Velagici.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes. I found out about that situation in the municipal building in the office of the president of the municipality who was the president of the Crisis Staff at the same time. In the early evening hours, I was in the municipality building and there were other people there too. Among them, President Banjac was there and Colonel Galic. Colonel Galic asked President Banjac to make it possible for him to have the director of the company that had buses and transported passengers come to that office, and that did happen, and Colonel Galic asked him to provide two buses and to send them to Velagici to take over the detainees -- I mean, to have the detainees transported on these buses to Manjaca. The director of transport left, he sent two buses, and half an hour later two bus drivers walked into the office and stated that in Velagici they found people who had been killed. Colonel Galic was very surprised. He jumped up and he swore at that moment. So it was in that way and then that I found out that that had happened in Velagici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you hear or have knowledge of any other directions that Colonel Galic gave in respect to what had happened and any instructions for further measures?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Colonel Galic immediately ordered the arrest of the persons who had been guarding the school. They were handed over to the prosecutor's office, the military prosecutor's office, I don't know what the name was then, and these people were tried for what they did in Velagici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And subsequent to this, what information did the Crisis Staff receive in follow-up as to these perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: As for the arrested persons, the information we had was that prosecution was under way and that things were taking their course. And, of course, I had no further information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you on behalf of General Mladic and my team for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that finishes our direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. I suggest, Mr. Traldi, that we take a break first and that you will then have the first half-hour of your cross-examination after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We would like to see you back. We'll not finish your -- to hear your evidence today, but we have half an hour left after the break. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could see whether there is still some time remaining for the Court agenda. I'd like to deal with -- no, let's way until we get a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kalabic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You'll find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've previously testified as a Defence witness in the Brdjanin and Karadzic cases here at the ICTY; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you testified as a defence witness in the Lukic and Adamovic case in the Bosnian state court; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that you told the truth in those testimonies?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I have already said that my evidence is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to go now briefly through the positions you held during the war. You were a member of the Bosnian assembly, as you say in your statement. You were also a member of the Assembly of the Serbian Republic in Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were a member of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mentioned on direct examination that you were a member of the Kljuc Crisis Staff. You were also a member of the Kljuc War Presidency which was formed on the 10th of July, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff is the same thing as the War Presidency, except the name was changed. And, yes, I was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, members of the military, the VRS, would attend meetings of that Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Sometimes but not always.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's ask about a couple of people specifically. First, you mentioned being at a meeting with Colonel Galic. During the period from the 27th of May to the 1st of June, Colonel Galic would attend Crisis Staff meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: From time to time, he did attend meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Where was he based during that period?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: He was based in the Kula barracks, the municipality of Mrkonjic Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. During those few days from the 27th of May to the 1st of June, after he had come to Kljuc, where was he based?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, I would see him only in the office of the president of the municipality. I did not see him elsewhere. I don't know whether he had any particular headquarters in the municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you would sometimes attend meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, once or perhaps two times. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your recollection is that the president of Kljuc, Jovo Banjac, was a member of the ARK Crisis Staff as president; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Crisis Staff of the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And his duty as president of Kljuc and a member of the ARK Crisis Staff, one of his duties was to inform the Kljuc Crisis Staff about the ARK Crisis Staff's work and its decisions; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: That's the way it was supposed to be. However, the president very rarely attended these meetings. Or, rather, to the best of my knowledge. Perhaps he attended meetings of the Crisis Staff just a few times, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you do recall that it was his duty to inform members of the Kljuc Crisis Staff of decisions passed by the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, he was supposed to provide information to all members of the Crisis Staff, I mean, about the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- one of the previous answers leaves a question open. You said, talking about Mr. Banjac, you said: "Perhaps he attended meetings of the Crisis Staff just a few times, not more than that." Now immediately before that, you were talking about his position as a member of the Crisis Staff of the ARK and as a member of the Crisis Staff of Kljuc. When you said he attended meetings of the Crisis Staff just a few times, did you refer to the ARK Crisis Staff, or did you refer to the Kljuc Crisis Staff, or to both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was the Crisis Staff he attended only a few times. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, before the war you also sometimes attended the sessions of the SDS Main Board in Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't a member of the SDS Main Board, and I cannot remember whether I was present, perhaps once or twice, at a meeting of the SDS Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 31813, page 64.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I bring to counsel's attention, e-court says that this is under seal. I don't know why it would be, but that's what the description says in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Without going into the reasons, I can say this is Mr. Kalabic's testimony in the Karadzic case given without protective measures but with some limited portions in private session. I had checked beforehand and this wasn't one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic is -- we are thanking Mr. Ivetic for drawing the attention to it and apparently you have considered it thoroughly. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I thank Mr. Ivetic for the reminder as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were asked here by Mr. Karadzic, beginning at line 6: "Did you go to the sessions of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party in Sarajevo?" And you answered: "Seldom. The president of the municipal board of the SDS usually was there" -- sorry, "usually went there. I was someone -- sometimes there but it was not very frequently." Do you stand by the testimony you gave in the Karadzic case that you did sometimes attend sessions of the Main Board of the SDS in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Can you show me the document? I'd like to know what exactly I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is your testimony in the Karadzic case. The transcript is only in English. I'm asking you: Do you stand by the sworn testimony you gave just over a year ago that I've just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by the testimony I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so you sometimes attended sessions of the Main Board of the SDS in Sarajevo and usually the president of the Kljuc Municipal Board of the SDS went to those sessions; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the president of the Kljuc Municipal Board, who was that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: The president of the SDS Kljuc Municipal Board was Veljko Kondic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he would report back to the Kljuc SDS about what had happened at those sessions; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: If he attended a session, he would briefly report back on what had been concluded at such a session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to your evidence -- well, I want to turn to the topic of political developments before the war, and I want to start in December 1991. When you were in Sarajevo in December 1991, you saw a copy of the instructions for the organisation of the Serbian people; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that I ever saw a copy of the instruction for the organisation of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31814, page 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, this will be your sworn testimony in the Brdjanin case. Now, beginning at line 15, Mr. Brdjanin counsel, Mr. Ackerman, asked you: "You have a document, sir, at tab 27 of your book. The last document in your book. It's Exhibit P25. I've only got it there so that you can refresh your memory as to what it is. It's the Variant A and B document which you have seen. And I'll ask you if you've seen it before I showed it to you yesterday." And you answered: "Yes, I saw this document in Sarajevo." So I'll ask you again: Do you stand behind your sworn testimony in the Brdjanin trial as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: My testimony was correct and truthful, but it was a long time ago so I can't remember all the things that I said. Therefore, it would be good if I were presented with the things that you're asking me about on the screen in the Serbian language so as to jog my memory. All the time I'm seeing something in English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there is no B/C/S version, and that's the reason why it's read out to you, and then it is interpreted by our interpreters, and then you receive it in your own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- I believe the witness is talking about the document, the Variant A and B document, which was described as instructions by Mr. Traldi which is referred to as Variant A and B document in this transcript. He's asking to see that document so that he can know which documents he's being asked if he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to call it up. Could we have P03038.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the number, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, seeing these instructions on the screen and having been reminded of your testimony in the Brdjanin case, does that refresh your recollection as to whether, in fact, you saw this document in Sarajevo in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I saw the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the document was then given to representatives of the SDS who brought these instructions back to their respective municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't know if they were all given it, but I know that the president of the SDS, Veljko Kondic, was in charge of that. So he was the one who had it, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So who gave Veljko Kondic a copy of this document to take back to Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. However, I suppose it was done by the services of -- administrative services of the party organs. I didn't really follow the goings on, who got it and who didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you said you saw it in Sarajevo. Were you present when it was given to him, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can the Prosecution please have MFI P7003. As -- and this will be a shorthand record of the 4th Session of the RS Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, you mentioned Mr. Kondic but clearly he wasn't the only representative of the SDS who was given this to take back to their municipality. You said you don't know if they were all given it but you know that many members of the SDS received this and took it back to their municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who got it, whether many got it, how many got it. I really don't know. I didn't see it. It was not my task to monitor those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, this is the 4th Session of the RS Assembly, and I'll turn to it now. It was also held while you were in the Sarajevo in December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 26 in the English, 55 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here Vukic speaking. This is Radislav Vukic, one of the other political leaders in the Autonomous Region of the Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't remember Radislav Vukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 27 in the English and 56 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Vukic says at the end of his remarks: "The Serbian people of Bosnian Krajina and Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole are part of the Serbian nation in Yugoslavia and as a constituent nation they are not going to accept any decision on which state they are going to live in without their consent, especially not this majoritarian illegal decision made by the other two nations. If the EC goes on with its threat to recognise Bosnia and Herzegovina as an independent state or as part of a future Independent State of Croatia, or the Independent State of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there will be another Serbian uprising and there will be massive bloodshed in which some nations that have been subsequently created, will disappear altogether. Thank you." And the transcript records there was applause. Now, when Mr. Vukic is referring here to nations that have been subsequently created, I put to you he means Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know Mr. Vukic. I can't remember of anybody delivering such a speech; therefore, I can't make any inferences as to what they thought if they said what you say they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What -- of the three nations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croats, the Muslims, the Serbs, was one of those three described by Serb leaders as having been subsequently or recently created?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't know who they meant if they spoke like this, which people or peoples they had in mind. I don't know. I'm not in a position to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir, how old is the Serb nation in your view?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I've never been interested in the issue at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And how long had a census category and one of the constituent peoples in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer can only be arbitrary. I can't give you a correct answer to your question. I'm in no position to answer such questions of yours with any accuracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's see if you're in a position to answer they question. Mr. Vukic says a nation is going to disappear altogether in massive bloodshed if there is a declaration of independence and then people applaud. People would not have applauded if he had -- or if they'd understood him to mean the Serbs were going to disappear; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am going to object. If counsel's going to refer to a document, counsel should cite to the document correctly, not giving a free-hand interpretation of what the document actually says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please quote literally, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "If the EC goes on with its threat to recognise Bosnia-Herzegovina as an independent state or as part of a future Independent State of Croatia or the Independent State of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there will be another Serbian uprising and there will be massive bloodshed in which some nations that have been subsequently created will disappear altogether. Thank you. (Applause)." So I put to you again, no one would have applauded if they thought Mr. Vukic meant that the Serbs were going to disappear; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: I don't remember this kind of speech --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Mladic, you now two times spoke aloud. Now you are standing, which you're supposed not to do. This is the last warning. If you want to consult with counsel, you can do so now but at an inaudible volume level. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, as a deputy in the assembly, part of your role, parallel to Mr. Kondic's, was to go back to Kljuc and report on what happened at the RS Assembly sessions; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: No, the president of the SDS Municipal Board was in charge of that, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll see if I can refresh your recollection, but I'm going to have to do it tomorrow. In the meantime, I'd put to you: You, in fact, reported to the Kljuc SDS about what happened at this particular assembly session, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think that's a good place to break and pick up in the morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn for the day, Mr. Kalabic. But I'd first like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, that is testimony you've given today, or that is testimony still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. You may follow the usher now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 20th of January, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of January, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
